A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Model Swarms study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, reward-model adaptation, human evaluations, and ablation and robustness analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark tables, human evaluations, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same initialization, velocity and weight updates, restart rule, and stopping procedure. Token swarms, dropout acceleration, and expert addition/removal procedures are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training data, nine single-task benchmarks, four multi-task domains, reward-model objectives, and sixteen human-interest topics. Appendix test scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments: the twelve composition baselines in Table 1, PPO/DPO in the reward-model comparison, and SFT in Table 9 all remain.

E3.justification: Sections 3 and Appendix C retain the same models, training settings, search budgets, data splits, metrics, decoding procedures, and human-evaluation design. Table 10 preserves the dataset-specific sample counts.

E4.justification: Randomness ablations, dropout acceleration, search trajectories, and weak-expert comparisons move from Section 5 to Appendix B without substantive changes. The existing component ablations, sensitivity tests, prompt-variation analysis, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain the same run-count disclosures, run-variance plots, Table 8 means and standard deviations, Table 10 one-tailed z-tests, and human-annotation Fleiss' kappa of 0.62.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains Model Swarms test scores of 0.583 on MMLU and 0.459 on GSM8k. The reward-model and human-interest tables exchange numbers 3 and 4, but preserve their results; appendix results and examples also match.

T1.justification: The update equations, correctness-surge/emergence definitions, complexity analysis, and Appendix B expert-removal derivation remain mathematically unchanged. Equation wrapping changes only their presentation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about tuning-free adaptation, low-data operation, performance across four adaptation objectives, emerging capabilities, and weak-to-strong expert transitions.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are retained, including expert diversity, computational cost, difficulty learning unseen information, architecture constraints, local minima, and misuse risks. Renaming the limitations section to Impact Statement does not change its substance.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit repository link advertised for code and data in the abstract; v1 only promises a future link. Implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, preprocessing, and evaluation instructions remain unchanged, and v2 still retains the older future-release wording.

R1.justification: The cited research and positioning relative to model composition, evolutionary optimization, and multi-agent systems are unchanged. Bibliographic formatting and author-year suffix changes refer to the same works.

P1.justification: v2 moves four existing analysis discussions from Section 5 into Appendix B and renames the limitations heading. Small prose, affiliation, and acknowledgement edits accompany this localized reorganization; most wording and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts an ICML two-column layout, extensively resizing and repositioning existing figures, tables, and equations. Several analysis displays move into Appendix B, and Tables 3 and 4 exchange numbering. A long normalization fraction on v2 page 20 intrudes into the adjacent text column.

improvement.justification: The explicit code/data repository link provides a modest improvement in resource discoverability over v1's future-release promise. Scientific content and evidential support remain unchanged. The benefit is partly offset by the local equation overflow on v2 page 20 and retained outdated release wording, making the overall improvement limited.
